children: Meta Platforms META shares have been red-hot as of late, seeing big gains on the recent release of Muse, Meta's personal AI assistant that can autonomously complete multi-step tasks across the web, apps, and smart glasses. It marks another major step in the AI race, with the company pushing beyond traditional chat-based assistants and deeper into agentic AI.
Shares have gained roughly 35% just in September.

Rather than simply responding to prompts, Muse is designed to complete complex, multi-step tasks on a user’s behalf. The system can operate across the web, desktop applications, and connected personal accounts, handling tasks from cross-referencing travel plans to completing e-commerce purchases.

The rollout has generated plenty of attention, particularly given the tedious tasks it can potentially take off users’ plates. Early use cases have included filing flight compensation claims and dealing with customer service calls, highlighting the broader opportunity for agentic AI to handle real-world tasks rather than simply provide information.

Meta is also extending Muse into its wearable ecosystem. Integrating the technology into its AI-powered glasses pushes the agentic opportunity even further, potentially allowing users to interact with what they see and hear in real time without needing to pull out a phone or sit behind a computer.

Still, the deeper integration naturally brings concerns. Privacy and security remain key issues given the level of access required to personal email, messaging histories, and local files, with broader questions surrounding permissions and data handling likely to remain in focus as adoption grows.

Overall, Muse reflects Meta’s continued push deeper into AI, with the company looking beyond chatbots and toward agents that can actually take action on users’ behalf. The opportunity is undoubtedly massive, though execution, privacy, and the ability to reliably automate increasingly complex tasks will remain key aspects to watch as the technology develops.
